core_obligations: Choose generators f_1, ..., f_r of I and denote by C^bullet_A -> C^bullet_B the quasi-isomorphism of extended alternating Cech complexes (proof lines 26643-26646).

For K in D_comp(A, I) represented by a K-injective complex I^bullet of A-modules, use the vanishing of Ext^n_A(A_f, K) and Ext^n_A(B_f, K) for all f in I and all n to conclude that C^bullet_A -> A and C^bullet_B -> B induce the two displayed quasi-isomorphisms; the author states that some details are omitted (proof lines 26647-26662).
Since C^bullet_A -> C^bullet_B is a quasi-isomorphism and I^bullet is K-injective, conclude that Hom_A(B, I^bullet) -> I^bullet is a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 26663-26665).
Use that Hom_A(B, I^bullet) is a complex of B-modules to conclude that K lies in the image of the restriction functor, giving essential surjectivity (proof lines 26666-26669).
Observe that the argument exhibits F : D_comp(A, I) -> D_comp(B, IB), K -> Hom_A(B, I^bullet), as a left inverse to restriction (proof lines 26671-26672).

For L in D_comp(B, IB) represented by a K-injective complex J^bullet of B-modules, use that J^bullet is also K-injective as a complex of A-modules to conclude F(restriction of L) = Hom_A(B, J^bullet), and use the map J^bullet -> Hom_A(B, J^bullet) of complexes of B-modules whose composite with Hom_A(B, J^bullet) -> J^bullet is the identity to conclude that F is also a right inverse, finishing the proof (proof lines 26673-26683).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring map A -> B and a finitely generated ideal I contained in A, assumes that A -> B is flat and that A/I is isomorphic to B/IB, and concludes that the restriction functor D(B) -> D(A) induces an equivalence D_comp(B, IB) -> D_comp(A, I) (source lines 26634-26640). The proof exhibits an explicit inverse. It chooses generators f_1, ..., f_r of I and uses the quasi-isomorphism of extended alternating Cech complexes C^bullet_A -> C^bullet_B; for K in D_comp(A, I) represented by a K-injective complex I^bullet of A-modules, it uses the vanishing of Ext^n_A(A_f, K) and Ext^n_A(B_f, K) for all f in I and all n to conclude that both C^bullet_A -> A and C^bullet_B -> B induce quasi-isomorphisms, in a step the author states is omitted (proof lines 26643-26662). Since C^bullet_A -> C^bullet_B is a quasi-isomorphism and I^bullet is K-injective, the proof concludes that Hom_A(B, I^bullet) -> I^bullet is a quasi-isomorphism, and because Hom_A(B, I^bullet) is a complex of B-modules this shows K is in the image of the restriction functor, i.e. essential surjectivity (proof lines 26663-26669). The argument in fact exhibits F : D_comp(A, I) -> D_comp(B, IB), K -> Hom_A(B, I^bullet), as a left inverse to restriction (proof lines 26671-26672). The final step shows F is also a right inverse: for L in D_comp(B, IB) represented by a K-injective complex J^bullet of B-modules, J^bullet is also K-injective as a complex of A-modules, so F applied to the restriction of L gives Hom_A(B, J^bullet), and there is a map J^bullet -> Hom_A(B, J^bullet) of complexes of B-modules whose composite with Hom_A(B, J^bullet) -> J^bullet is the identity (proof lines 26673-26683). The non-routine content is the systematic use of Cech complexes and K-injectivity to build the two-sided inverse.
